notes:
Recorded under the owner's v0.17 assurance-closure mandate of 2026-09-07, priority 2: investigate mcp-re-host's four zero-test files, especially signer.rs and nonce.rs, identify security-bearing propositions, add controls for genuine evidence gaps, register the smallest honest owners. Recorded by the implementing agent as routine owner-review maintenance, not as a transcription of a ruling naming this fingerprint.

THE MEASUREMENT CHANGED WHAT THE SLICE IS ABOUT. signer.rs is DORMANT: HostSigner has no consumer anywhere — not the deployable client, not the client proxy, not either SDK, not a test, not the demo surface. Every real signing site calls mcp_re_client_core::build_signed_request directly, and the ADR-MCPS-003 property HostSigner documents — a private key with no accessor — is held on the live path by mcp_re_client_proxy::McpReProxy, whose signing_key field is private and which client.proxy_request_correspondence owns under THM-0084. Excluded from this unit on the precedent that kept trust_plane/window_policy.rs and async_replay/l1_fast_reject.rs out of theirs. It was given controls for the code standard and is cited by nothing; retiring a documented signing-locus expression is an architectural decision and not an audit's to take, so it is recorded as a finding rather than deleted. mcp-re-client's own manifest says what the crate is actually used for: the clock and the OS-CSPRNG nonce source.

A CONTROL FOUND A REAL PRODUCTION BUG. clock.rs computed a pre-epoch reading as `(secs as i64).checked_neg().unwrap_or(i64::MIN)`, and its comment claimed i64::MIN was the answer for magnitudes past the boundary. It is not: (2^63 + 1) as i64 wraps to i64::MIN + 1, whose negation is i64::MAX. A clock set unrepresentably far BEFORE the epoch reported the furthest instant in the FUTURE — which every freshness window accepts, and which is precisely the fabricated plausible time the comment says must never happen. Unreachable on a real host, and the code claimed a property it did not have. Fixed with try_from, so the magnitude is refused before it is negated; the boundary control now spans 2^63-1 through u64::MAX. The arithmetic was extracted to a pure function first, because a SystemTimeError is not constructible and a control over now_unix could never have reached that arm at all.

A SECOND CONTROL MEASURED THE CARRIER. The signer controls first used a short nonce label and were refused: the RFC 9421 carrier enforces the 128-bit entropy floor at signing. That is the floor holding, measured rather than assumed.

THE FIXTURE BOUNDARY GOT ITS OWN OWNER. Audit #81 made the deterministic fixtures an ENFORCED boundary, and it has two halves that fail independently: the #[cfg] on each item, and the feature not being default. A `default = ["test-fixtures"]` would satisfy every #[cfg] in the crate with no source line changing, and a non-dev self-dependency would do the same for every downstream consumer. Both are now controlled, from the source and the manifest that are actually built (include_str!, at compile time), in fixture_boundary.rs — a module with no production item, because the fact is a property of the crate's build configuration and neither of the two modules whose types it protects can state it about the other. Cargo.toml is a unit path for exactly that reason.

THE CRATE HAD NO BAZEL TEST TARGET AT ALL, so the Bazel lane said nothing about it. One was added over the test-fixtures flavor.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: nothing about what is signed or whether a request verifies; nothing about the OS CSPRNG itself — the distinctness control is statistical over 64 draws, not a randomness test; nothing about a third party's Clock or NonceSource implementation, only that THESE fixtures stay off the default surface; and nothing about HostSigner.
